kurz: Understand these ten processes and you understand most of what happens when you cook and bake.
fuer: For anyone who wants to start with the fundamentals

schritte.warum: Where it all begins: as long as there is water, nothing gets hotter than 100 °C.
How heat gets into food at all, and why the outside cooks faster than the inside.
From 140 °C you get what we love as the smell of roasting and a brown crust.
The Maillard reaction's relative: sugar on its own turns brown and aromatic.
Why meat, fish and eggs cook through, and why they turn dry when cooked too long.
The opposite: tough meat needs time until its connective tissue melts.
What thickens sauces, softens potatoes and makes risotto creamy.
How oil and water hold together: mayonnaise, vinaigrette, hollandaise.
The network in dough that makes bread rise and can make cake tough.
Why salt draws out water, and what that means for when to salt.

quiz.frage: Why does a wet steak not brown in a hot pan?
antworten: As long as water evaporates, the surface stays at about 100 °C
Water stops the salt from working
quiz.erklaerung: Browning only starts at around 140 °C. As long as there is water, the surface cannot get hotter than that.

quiz.frage: At roughly what temperature does the Maillard reaction really get going?
quiz.erklaerung: From about 140 °C, protein and sugar building blocks combine into roasted flavours.

quiz.frage: Why does a tough braising cut turn tender after hours?
antworten: The collagen in the connective tissue turns into gelatine
The muscle fibres are boiled soft
quiz.erklaerung: Connective tissue slowly dissolves into gelatine in moist heat. That takes time, not more heat.

quiz.frage: What holds a mayonnaise together?
antworten: The emulsifier in the egg yolk
quiz.erklaerung: Lecithin and protein from the yolk coat the oil droplets and keep them apart.

quiz.frage: What happens when shortcrust pastry is kneaded for too long?
antworten: It turns tough because gluten forms
quiz.erklaerung: Kneading links the proteins into gluten. You want that in bread; in shortcrust it makes the pastry tough.

quiz.frage: Why does a sauce with cornflour only thicken once it boils briefly?
antworten: Starch only swells in the heat
quiz.erklaerung: Starch granules only take up water and swell from about 60–70 °C. Cold, almost nothing happens.

kurz: Twelve experiments where you see, smell and taste what happens in the kitchen. With adults at the stove and hot water.
fuer: For children from about 8, together with adults

schritte.warum: Colour magic to start with: red cabbage juice shows whether something is acidic.
Why the apple turns brown, and how to stop it.
Salt draws out water: you can actually watch it happen.
What makes the bubbles in a cake.
Yeast is alive and breathes: it blows up a balloon.
A tiny drop of fat ruins a whole bowl of egg whites.
Cream turns into butter, just by shaking.
Make ice cream in ten minutes with ice and salt.
Fresh pineapple cuts up the jelly.
The invisible network in flour becomes visible.
Why vegetables turn grey when they cook too long.
To finish, an experiment over several days: growing crystals.

quiz.frage: Red cabbage juice turns pink. What did you add?
quiz.erklaerung: Acid such as vinegar turns the red cabbage pigment pink; baking soda turns it blue to green.

quiz.frage: Why does an apple slice with lemon juice stay pale?
antworten: The acid slows down the enzyme that turns the apple brown
quiz.erklaerung: An enzyme in the apple makes brown pigments with air. Acid slows it down.

quiz.frage: After 15 minutes there are drops of water on salted cucumber slices. Where does the water come from?
quiz.erklaerung: Salt draws water out of the cucumber's cells. This is called osmosis.

quiz.frage: What blows up the balloon on the yeast bottle?
antworten: Carbon dioxide made by the yeast
quiz.erklaerung: Yeast eats sugar and breathes out carbon dioxide. The same gas makes the holes in bread.

quiz.frage: Why won't egg whites with a drop of yolk whip up stiff?
antworten: The fat in the yolk makes the air bubbles burst
quiz.erklaerung: Fat pushes in between the thin protein skins around the bubbles, and they burst.

quiz.frage: Why does milk in a bag turn into ice cream with ice and salt, but not with ice alone?
antworten: Salt makes the ice even colder
quiz.erklaerung: Salt makes the ice melt, and the brine gets far colder than 0 °C. That is cold enough to freeze the milk.

quiz.frage: Why does jelly with fresh pineapple stay runny?
antworten: An enzyme in pineapple cuts up the gelatine
quiz.erklaerung: Gelatine is a protein. The enzyme in fresh pineapple cuts its network apart. Tinned pineapple has been heated, so its enzyme no longer works.

quiz.frage: What is the rubbery lump left over when you wash out dough?
quiz.erklaerung: The milky stuff in the water is starch. The tough lump is gluten, the network that holds the air in bread.

kurz: From flour to crust: what happens in a loaf, and which levers you can turn.
fuer: For anyone who wants to bake their own bread
dauer: about 1 hour of reading, then practice

schritte.warum: What is in flour: starch, protein and a few enzymes.
The network that holds the gas bubbles.
Why a little rest can replace kneading.
Who supplies the gas, and how temperature slows it down or speeds it up.
More time gives more flavour.
Structure without kneading.
Why steam in the first minutes makes the loaf bigger.
The crust.
Why bread goes stale, and how to refresh it.
The next step: starting your own sourdough.

quiz.frage: What holds the gas bubbles in bread dough?
quiz.erklaerung: Gluten forms a stretchy network that holds the bubbles like little balloons.

quiz.frage: Why does a dough proved cold overnight develop more flavour?
antworten: Over time, more flavour compounds and sugars form
quiz.erklaerung: Slow fermentation and enzymes have more time. That gives flavour and a browner crust.

quiz.frage: What is steam good for in the first minutes in the oven?
antworten: The crust stays soft for a while, so the loaf can still rise
quiz.erklaerung: A moist surface stays stretchy. That way the loaf can still grow before the crust sets.

quiz.frage: Why does bread go stale faster in the fridge?
antworten: The starch reorganises faster in the cold
quiz.erklaerung: Stale means the starch crystallises again. That happens much faster in the fridge.

quiz.frage: What does a sourdough do differently from yeast alone?
antworten: It brings lactic acid bacteria for acidity and flavour
quiz.erklaerung: In a sourdough, wild yeasts and lactic acid bacteria work together.

kurz: Juicy, tender, with a crust: the principles behind steak, roasts and braises.
fuer: For anyone who no longer wants to cook meat by feel

schritte.warum: What happens in meat as it cooks, degree by degree.
The most important number, and why a thermometer helps more than any rule of thumb.
Salt the day before: juicier and better seasoned.
No crust without a dry surface.
What goes wrong when the pan is too full or too cold.
What resting really does, with measurements.
Why tough cuts slowly turn tender.
The technique for it.
What to watch out for with poultry and leftovers.
Everything together: a pan-fried steak.

quiz.frage: From what point do the muscle fibres contract strongly and squeeze out juice?
quiz.erklaerung: From about 66 °C a second protein contracts strongly. That is why meat dries out quickly above this point.

quiz.frage: What does salting meat the day before do?
antworten: It turns juicier and the surface dries
quiz.erklaerung: The salt soaks in and helps the meat hold on to water. The surface dries and browns better.

quiz.frage: Why does meat turn grey instead of brown when there is too much in the pan?
antworten: The pan cools down and the meat stews in its own juices
The meat was salted too cold
quiz.erklaerung: A lot of meat releases a lot of juice. The pan loses heat and the surface gets stuck at 100 °C.

quiz.frage: How hot must poultry get at its core, at the very least?
quiz.erklaerung: For poultry, food safety authorities recommend at least 70 °C at the core for two minutes.

quiz.frage: Why does a braise turn more tender the longer it cooks?
quiz.erklaerung: Connective tissue needs moist heat and time to turn into gelatine.

kurz: Almost every sauce is an emulsion, thickened with starch, or reduced. Know the three ways and you can rescue any sauce.
fuer: For anyone whose sauce has ever split or come out too thin

schritte.warum: The overview: three ways to thicken a sauce.
Way 1: fat in water as tiny droplets.
The emulsion to make yourself.
What to do when it splits.
Way 2: starch swells and thickens.
The classic technique for it.
Way 3: reduce until it turns smooth and thick.
Cold butter at the end: shine and body.
The master class: a warm emulsion with egg yolk.
For emergencies.

quiz.frage: What are the three ways to thicken a sauce?
quiz.erklaerung: Almost every sauce is an emulsion, thickened with starch, or reduced.

quiz.frage: Your mayonnaise splits. What helps?
antworten: Take a fresh egg yolk and slowly whisk in the split sauce
quiz.erklaerung: The fresh yolk brings new emulsifier. Worked in slowly, the emulsion forms again.

quiz.frage: Why does cold butter go into the sauce at the end?
antworten: To give it shine and body
quiz.erklaerung: Cold butter melts slowly and spreads out in fine droplets: the sauce turns glossy and smooth.

quiz.frage: What happens when hollandaise gets too hot?
antworten: The egg yolk sets and the sauce turns lumpy
quiz.erklaerung: Egg yolk starts to set from about 70 °C. That is why hollandaise is made over a water bath and kept warm, not hot.

quiz.frage: Why do you salt a sauce that still needs reducing only at the end?
antworten: Reducing concentrates the salt as well
quiz.erklaerung: The water evaporates, the salt stays. Salt it early and the sauce ends up too salty.

kurz: From shortcrust to gingerbread: why biscuits turn tender, glossy, soft or crisp, and how they stay that way.
fuer: For anyone baking in Advent, children included
dauer: about 1 hour of reading, then bake

schritte.warum: Almost all biscuits are shortcrust: fat between the flour makes them tender.
Why biscuit dough is barely kneaded but bread dough for a long time.
Cold dough holds its shape: the most important step when cutting out.
All of it together in the classic, with an egg-yolk sheen.
Bake pale and glue with pectin.
Whisked egg white as a building material: for glazes and flourless biscuits.
Why the glaze stays white only in a cool oven.
Short and hot: firm outside, soft inside.
A dry skin plus steam makes the feet.
What else besides yeast lightens doughs.
Honey, baker's ammonia and a long rest.
So the work lasts until Christmas.
To finish: yeast dough for St Nicholas Day.

quiz.frage: Why is biscuit dough kneaded only briefly?
antworten: So the butter does not melt
So little gluten forms and the biscuits stay short
So the sugar does not dissolve
quiz.erklaerung: Kneading builds the gluten network. Good for bread, but it makes biscuits tough.

quiz.frage: Why chill cut-out biscuits again before baking?
antworten: So the edges set before the butter melts
quiz.erklaerung: Cold butter melts more slowly in the oven, so the shapes stay sharp.

quiz.frage: Why are cinnamon stars baked at a low temperature?
antworten: So the almonds do not melt
So the egg-white and sugar glaze does not brown
So the cinnamon does not burn
quiz.erklaerung: Protein and sugar brown in heat. Baked cool, the glaze stays white.

quiz.frage: Where do Chräbeli get their feet?
antworten: From baking powder in the dough
The dry skin on top holds, and the dough swells out underneath
quiz.erklaerung: Overnight a sugar skin dries on top. In the oven the inside expands and can only escape underneath.

quiz.frage: Why does an apple slice keep gingerbread soft?
antworten: The apple gives off moisture, and honey and sugar take it up
The acid in the apple dissolves the sugar
quiz.erklaerung: Honey and sugar draw in moisture. The apple supplies it in the closed tin.
